text.p: Italian bond futures continued easier in late trading reflecting stronger U.S. Treasuries and as German bunds recovered, but trading was lacklustre with many operators still wary of investing in Italy, dealers said.

Italian bonds took their lead from the U.S., tumbling early on overnight T-bond weakness and then paring back losses as the U.S. began a recovery despite a strong rise in U.S. August consumer confidence figures this afternoon.
The LIFFE September contract halved its losses from earlier while Milan futures, which showed big losses on Monday while London was closed for a UK bank holiday, saw small gains.

The Italian market was troubled on Monday by a debate over Italy's committment to European political and monetary union which involved members of the Italian cabinet, but Prime Minister Romano Prodi stressed Italy will hold firm on its determination to pursue the goal of a European currency union.
Dealers said that this debate hit sentiment across Italy's financial markets and left international investors very wary of moving into Italy.
"The market is trying to steady, but we could be set for another plunge below 115 as the budget debate begins to gather momentum," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers said that investors still had an eye on the passage of Italy's 1997 financial budget through parliament starting next month, and further problems for the centre-left government this autumn on wage agreements and privatisation issues.
